incident-bot: PAGER: HIGH GPU UTILIZATION detected on cluster-realtime-01. queue_length=4200, avg_latency=1800ms, error_rate=12% :rotating_light:
Maya (oncall-sre): I'm paged, looking. Confirming scope: are only realtime inference pools affected?
Alan (runtime): yes repro on /v1/generate and /v1/chat endpoints. Many 429s and long tails. Logs show OOM throttles and throttled-rps spikes.
Maya (oncall-sre): grabbing metrics dashboards. autoscaler events show multiple scale-up attempts failed with "max nodes reached" for nodepool gpu-pool-us-east-1.
Priya (infra): Confirmed. Nodepool gpu-pool-us-east-1 maxSize=40, current=40. Cluster autoscaler tried 5 times in last 10m.
Jeremy (eng-oncall): Is there an immediate mitigation to reduce customer impact? Can we shift traffic to smaller models or non-GPU fallback?
Alan (runtime): We have a compatible quantized CPU fallback (model-q6a-cpu) but throughput will be lower; can route non-SLA customers to it. Need quick routing rule and rate-limit changes.
Maya (oncall-sre): Plan: 1) Apply emergency routing to move non-enterprise traffic to cpu fallback. 2) Enable request-level throttling (soft 60 rps per org). 3) Request manual nodepool cap increase from infra/cloud.
Sam (cust-success): Heads-up — a few enterprise customers already reported degraded responses. I'll draft a status note once we confirm mitigation window.
Priya (infra): I'm on it. Filing manual support/console increase request to raise gpu-pool maxSize to 80. ETA from cloud portal is ~10-25m for pool resize permission check. Meanwhile we can also spin up a second nodepool if needed but will require nodepool config and taints.
Maya (oncall-sre): Executing step 1 now: adding routing rule to route org tier != enterprise to model-q6a-cpu. Patch in router: `PATCH /router/policies` with small rule, pushing in 2s.
ops-bot: deploy started: router/policies patch 7ad3f.. -> rolling 3 replicas
Alan (runtime): Routing patch applied. I'm seeing immediate drop in GPU queue length for non-enterprise traffic from 4200 -> 1600. Good. GPU backlog still high for enterprise workloads.
Jeremy (eng-oncall): Can we temporarily increase per-customer token limits and enforce queue priority? We should protect enterprise SLAs.
Maya (oncall-sre): Enabled priority queueing: enterprise gets high priority with preemptible slots. Non-enterprise now in CPU fallback queue.
Sam (cust-success): Notifying affected customers: drafted message: "We're mitigating elevated latencies by routing to fallback models; enterprise customers prioritized. Expect improvements in 10-30m." Ready to send after Priya confirms capacity raise.
Priya (infra): Cloud console request submitted (ticket #CLD-11472). Also opened support chat asking for accelerated pool resize. Manual increase to 80 accepted pending billing/quotas check — currently they flagged GPU quota limit in the account, escalating.
Maya (oncall-sre): Observability update: avg_latency now 950ms overall, enterprise tail 2xx0ms. Error rate dropping from 12% -> 6% after routing.
Alan (runtime): We're still seeing autoscaler events complaining about pod resource requests vs max pods per node. A few pods refused due to `maxPodsPerNode` hitting kubelet limit. Need to consider node sizing or reduce per-pod `requests.cpu/memory` or convert some pods to sidecar-less variants.
Jeremy (eng-oncall): Can we temporarily reduce per-pod request to allow more pods per node? Risky but could help while infra increases nodes.
Maya (oncall-sre): I'll patch a lower request profile for the realtime jobset (from 12G to 8G GPU mem reservation) for non-critical replicas. Alan — can you validate that the runtime tolerates lower reservation?
Alan (runtime): Quick test on staging shows model processes accept reduced reserve on newer runtime, but there's slight increase in OOM risk for long sequences. We'll limit that to non-enterprise replicas only.
Priya (infra): Cloud just messaged: quota team needs approval; they can raise GPU quota if we provide customer-impact justification and estimate. I'm filling that in — request to double gpu quota and extend nodepool max size to 100 as temporary relief.
Maya (oncall-sre): Sending impact statement: 3000+ queued requests, 20% of production requests getting >1.5s extra latency, multiple customers reporting errors. Requesting expedited raise.
ops-bot: ticket CLD-11472 updated with impact statement and request for urgent review.
Priya (infra): Support chat replies: provisional approval for quota raise pending billing check. ETA 18m. Meanwhile I've started a second nodepool `gpu-burst-01` with taints to accept only preemptible workloads; manual creation in progress.
Alan (runtime): Creating placeholders: `kubectl create nodepool gpu-burst-01 --machine n1-standard-32 --gpus=8 --taint=dedicated=realtime:PreferNoSchedule` (mock). I'll update the runtime mapping when nodes join.
Maya (oncall-sre): Observability: queue_length down to 900, overall error_rate 3.1%, enterprise tail still noisy but improving.
Sam (cust-success): Sending status update to affected customers now (brief note + ETA 30m).
Priya (infra): Cloud quota increase completed: GPU quota doubled, nodepool maxSize updated to 100. Nodes starting; expected join in 6-9 minutes.
Maya (oncall-sre): Great. Once nodes join we'll remove the emergency lower request patch and rebalance pods back to GPU pool. Plan to rollback routing rule after traffic normalizes.
Alan (runtime): New nodes joined (3 nodes so far). Autoscaler back to healthy. I'm draining CPU-fallback replicas and reassigning enterprise traffic back to GPU replicas slowly.
Jeremy (eng-oncall): Any ongoing customer-visible errors?
Maya (oncall-sre): Error rate stabilized at 1.1%. Average latency 420ms. I'm going to mark the incident as mitigated and start handoff notes.
Sam (cust-success): Sent follow-up to customers: "Issue mitigated, we scaled capacity and routed non-SLA traffic to fallbacks. We will follow up with root cause and timeline".
Priya (infra): Postmortem action: increase default nodepool maxSize early warning when autoscaler attempts >80% for >5min. Also audit per-node `maxPods` and pod requests to avoid pod-scheduling failures.
Maya (oncall-sre): Handoff: oncall brigade — I'll leave runbook checklist and action items: 1) Confirm nodes stable for 2h, 2) Revert temporary request changes for non-enterprise after 1h, 3) Add autoscaler alert for "max nodes reached" (currently missing), 4) Prep cost estimate for extended nodepool size.
ops-bot: incident closed (mitigated) by Maya at 1752605650.
Maya (oncall-sre): Marking handoff to next oncall Jeremy. Please keep an eye on GPU backlog alert and the cloud quota ticket until it's fully closed.
Jeremy (eng-oncall): Acknowledged. I'll monitor dashboards and coordinate with infra for any billing approvals.
Sam (cust-success): I'll follow up with customers tomorrow with a detailed timeline and RCA once we have the postmortem.
Maya (oncall-sre): Quick notes for postmortem: suspected root causes = sudden organic traffic spike combined with autoscaler ceiling + conservative pod request profiles and kubelet `maxPods` limits. Mitigations applied = routing fallback, throttling, priority queueing, manual cap raise and nodepool burst. Action owners assigned in the incident doc.
Alan (runtime): I'll own the runtime-level improvements: graceful CPU fallback, adaptive request profiles, and a runtime metric to detect when per-pod requests block scheduling.
Priya (infra): I'll own infra actions: increase default pool max, add autoscaler alert, and coordinate with cloud for quota guardrails.
Maya (oncall-sre): Thanks all. Closing channel for further chatter — please continue updates in the incident doc and tag the postmortem PR when ready.
